rules.title: Prohibition on landlords using coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to coordinated pricing algorithms as defined in § 13.63.020 and to residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: The definition excludes certain aggregated anonymous reports that do not make recommendations; products used to establish affordable-housing rent or income limits; and specified market research, appraisal, and software-development research, testing, or training uses.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Do not inquire about criminal history
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not inquire about a current or prospective tenant’s criminal history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Berkeley rental housing; the summary lists exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; qualifying owner-occupied properties; certain units where the owner may move back; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: Inquire about criminal history

rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge no more than the stated maximum screening fee for 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: The document summarizes state and local screening-fee limits.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78; Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96

rules.title: Minimum rent debt required for nonpayment eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict for nonpayment unless the tenant’s rental debt equals or exceeds one month of the applicable fair market rent.
rules.key_value: At least one month of the applicable HUD Fair Market Rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code, Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

rules.title: Cap the Annual General Adjustment at 5%
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment may not exceed 5%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered Berkeley rental units; the cap does not prevent use of banked AGAs to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%.

rules.title: Pay adjusted standard relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Owners must pay relocation assistance for owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions; the 2026 standard payment is $19,413.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owner move-in evictions and evictions to remove a property from the rental housing market.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

rules.title: Security deposit interest coverage
rules.requirement: The guide indicates that listed fully and partially covered unit types are covered for security deposit interest.
rules.coverage_conditions: The table marks the listed fully and partially covered unit types as covered for security deposit interest.
rules.exemptions: The guide lists Golden Duplexes, certain owner-shared kitchen or bath units, certain ADU tenancies, university rental units, and nonprofit cooperatives as exempt.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

rules.title: No blanket criminal-record denials; individual review
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers must not impose a blanket policy denying housing to anyone with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants case by case.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span:
will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.

rules.title: Prohibit housing discrimination on protected grounds
rules.requirement: Discrimination is illegal in Boston when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for housing based on the listed protected characteristics.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing in the City of Boston.
rules.quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.

rules.title: Deliver tenant rights notice when ending tenancy
rules.requirement: When planning to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy, landlords and applicable foreclosing owners must provide the Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to the tenant or former owner at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of non-renewal.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities or health facilities, and residences in qualifying non-profit short-term treatment, assistance or therapy facilities for substance abuse.
rules.quoted_span:
The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction pro
rules.requirement: Pending bill: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Do not discriminate or harass in housing
rules.requirement: Housing providers must not discriminate against or harass tenants, residents, applicants, home seekers, or others because of a protected characteristic.
rules.exemptions: The document describes exceptions for certain owner-occupied shared housing and qualifying senior housing; see tenant conditions.
rules.quoted_span: This law prohibits people or entities that provide housing from discriminating against or harassing tenants, homeowners, residents, their guests, housing or mortgage applicants, home buyers, and others.

rules.title: Prohibition on algorithm use or distribution in a restraint of trade
rules.requirement: A person must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of the chapter.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Just cause required to terminate tenancy
rules.requirement: After the applicable continuous-occupancy period, an owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, and must state the cause in the written termination notice. Just cause includes the listed at-fault and no-fault grounds.
rules.coverage_conditions: Subject to the building and local-rule exclusions; the occupancy-duration threshold and qualifying cause are tenant/tenancy conditions.
rules.exemptions: Includes statutory exemptions for specified housing and circumstances, including qualifying local just-cause ordinances. Transient occupancy and owner-shared bathroom or kitchen facilities are circumstances not expressible as building facts.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Limit on rent increases
rules.requirement: An owner may not increase the gross rental rate during any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, calculated from the lowest gross rental rate charged during the prior 12 months. Accepted rent discounts, incentives, concessions, or credits are excluded from that lowest rate.
rules.key_value: 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living, capped at 10%, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to subsequent increases after an initial rental rate is established; subject to the statutory exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to specified affordable housing, educational dormitories, qualifying recently constructed housing, qualifying separately alienable property with required notice, qualifying owner-occupied duplexes, or mobilehome homeowners. Housing covered by stricter local rent controls yields to those local controls.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

rules.title: One-month security limit
rules.requirement: Except for the stated statutory exceptions, a landlord may not demand or receive security exceeding one month’s rent, in addition to first month’s rent paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.key_value: One month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.exemptions: The exceptions in paragraphs (2), (3), and (5) apply; this subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. The two-month limit in paragraph (5) does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent

rules.title: Limit on application screening fees
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee above the actual out-of-pocket costs and reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information, and the fee may not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to the stated annual CPI adjustment.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant; adjusted annually commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998
rules.quoted_span:
The amount of the application screening fee shall not be greater than the actual
out-of-pocket costs of gathering information concerning the applicant, including, but not limited to, the cost of using a tenant screening service or a consumer credit reporting service, and the reasonable value of time spent by the landlord or their agent in obtaining information on the applicant. In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Apply applicant-selection standards equally and uniformly
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents may use reasonable standards to select applicants only if they apply the standards equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing transactions in Cambridge.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.quoted_span: landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.title: Offer the tenants’ rights and resources Guide when taking legal steps to terminate a tenancy
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords, and management companies must offer the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including a single residential dwelling unit.
rules.exemptions: Rental units in specified health or nonprofit treatment facilities, and short-term rental units.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).

rules.title: Right to file an illegal rent petition
rules.requirement: A tenant who claims they are being charged illegal rent may file an Illegal Rent Petition.
rules.quoted_span: A tenant claiming the rent they are being charged is illegal may file an Illegal Rent Petition:

rules.title: Termination of tenancy requires just cause
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause; the JCO applies after the tenant has lived in the unit for at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO; the JCO may cover newer buildings and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Specific exceptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, certain cooperatives and some government-owned properties.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause

rules.title: Rent increase frequency and allowable percentage
rules.requirement: For covered RSO units, rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent-increase percentage; the reported rate for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is 3%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Generally, rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, including listed covered property types and replacement units under LAMC § 151.28.
rules.exemptions: Condominium and townhome rent amounts are not regulated for tenancies commencing after December 31, 1995.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending bill: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: Prohibition on algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithmic rent setting.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Prohibition on local rent control
rules.requirement: Cities and towns may not enact, maintain, or enforce rent control, except as allowed for a city or town that accepts the chapter.
rules.exemptions: A city or town that accepts the chapter may adopt rent control regulation subject to the stated restrictions.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: No discriminatory denial of covered housing
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not refuse to rent, lease, sell, negotiate for sale, or otherwise deny or withhold covered accommodations on the listed protected grounds.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing described in subsection 6 as publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, or contiguously located.
rules.quoted_span: (a) to refuse to rent or lease or sell or negotiate for sale or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons such accommodations because of the race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, which shall not include persons whose sexual orientation involves minor children as the sex object, age, genetic information, ancestry, or marital status of such person or persons or because such person is a veteran or member of the armed forces, or because such person is blind, or hearing impaired or has any other handicap;

rules.title: Written 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment
rules.requirement: To determine a written lease for nonpayment of rent, the landlord must give the tenant written notice to quit at least 14 days before termination.
rules.quoted_span: fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease

rules.title: Limit on amounts charged at the start of a tenancy
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor may not require payment of amounts beyond the listed first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a compliant security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the purchase and installation cost of a key and lock. A fee in lieu of a deposit may be authorized by regulation subject to the stated requirements.
rules.key_value: Security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Limit on amounts required at the start of a tenancy
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or the lessor’s agent may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay an amount beyond the charges permitted by this subsection.
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Fee paid by the party that contracted with the broker
rules.requirement: A broker's fee may be paid only by the lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the broker.
rules.key_value: Only the party who originally engaged and contracted with the broker may pay the fee.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Do not require pre-offer applications that inquire about criminal records
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to complete an application that includes criminal-record inquiries before making a conditional offer, except for the specified methamphetamine-related conviction and lifetime sex-offender registration inquiries.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than four dwelling units are outside the act's definition of rental dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer

rules.title: Do not evaluate applicants using specified criminal records
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged or pardoned convictions, legally nullified convictions, juvenile delinquency adjudications, or sealed records, before or after a conditional offer.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than four dwelling units are outside the act's definition of rental dwelling unit.

rules.title: Do not publish categorical criminal-record exclusion advertisements
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not knowingly or purposefully publish an advertisement explicitly stating that applicants arrested or convicted of crimes will not be considered, except for the two specified criminal-history categories.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than four dwelling units are outside the act's definition of rental dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not knowingly or
purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that
explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant
who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses

rules.title: Do not require drug or alcohol tests or request treatment-facility consent
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than four dwelling units are outside the act's definition of rental dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not require an applicant
to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to
obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Application fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee exceeding the statutory limit to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, or to a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord who collects a security deposit may not collect more than one and one-half times one month’s rent.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request and allows 30 days for the law to apply.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent

rules.title: Thirty-year exemption from local rent control for newly constructed multiple dwellings
rules.requirement: Local rent control ordinances do not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years following completion of construction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings during the first 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.quoted_span:
newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: Rent increase may not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: Eviction and nonrenewal require good cause
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds in court.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties; stated exceptions are recorded as tenant conditions.
rules.exemptions: Possible exceptions include certain owner-occupied premises, transient or seasonal guests, and a specified family trust unit.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

rules.title: No discrimination in housing based on protected characteristics
rules.requirement: A landlord may not discriminate in housing on the bases of race, creed (religion), color, national origin, sex, gender identity or expression, marital status, civil union status, ancestry, actual or perceived physical or mental disability, nationality, affectional or sexual orientation, familial status, or domestic partner status.
rules.exemptions: The brochure states exceptions for certain owner-occupied two-family and one-family rentals; familial-status discrimination is excepted for housing for older persons.
rules.quoted_span:
The NJ Law Against Discrimination (LAD) prohibits
discrimination on the bases of race, creed (religion),
color, national origin, sex, gender identity or expression,
marital status, civil union status, ancestry, actual or
perceived physical or mental disability, nationality,
affectional or sexual orientation, familial status, and
domestic partner status.

rules.title: Performing a coordinating function prohibited
rules.requirement: A person may not perform a coordinating function.
rules.quoted_span: any person to perform a coordinating function.

rules.title: Just cause required for termination of tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. The listed at-fault and good-faith no-fault reasons define the just cause grounds; additional stated conditions apply to particular no-fault grounds.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies unless an exemption in § 98.0703 applies.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include affordable housing, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and the other circumstances specified in § 98.0703.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlords using algorithmic devices
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. The defined term excludes the specified reporting software and software used in accordance with affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.exemptions: The definition of algorithmic device excludes specified reporting software and software used to establish rates or income limits in accordance with affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Just cause required for eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a just-cause reason that is the dominant motive to evict a tenant. The listed reasons include nonpayment or habitual late payment, substantial breach, nuisance, illegal use, refusal of lawful access, specified owner or family occupancy, sale after an approved condominium conversion, demolition or rehabilitation, Ellis Act withdrawal, lead remediation, and specified development or temporary-tenancy circumstances. Mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: The summary does not specify building-fact criteria for which units are covered. It states that some tenancies exempt from rent-increase limits remain subject to eviction protections.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: Annual rent increase limit: March 2026–February 2027
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.coverage_conditions: The summary identifies the covered units as rent-controlled but does not provide all building-fact criteria. It states that newly constructed rental units first obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from rent-increase limitations.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy prohibited
rules.requirement: A person may not use an algorithmic device to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. The described device analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend a rent for a vacant unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Security deposit interest rate: March 2026–February 2027
rules.requirement: The security deposit interest rate for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 4.2%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposit interest rate effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Limit on residential rent increases
rules.requirement: Limit annual rent increases to the lower of 3% or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period; if the CPI is negative, no increase is permitted.
rules.key_value: Lower of 3% per year or 80% of the CPI change; 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential buildings other than buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 and mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Just cause required to terminate tenancy
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Does not apply to housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels and transient occupancy, hospitals and care facilities, dormitories, or other shared living quarters.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause

rules.title: Ban on real estate lessors using service providers
rules.requirement: A real estate lessor, its agent, or its subcontractor may not subscribe to, contract with, or exchange anything of value for a service provider’s services.
rules.exemptions: The definition of “Coordinate” exempts owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same rental property owner. Licensed real estate agents operating in accordance with applicable state regulations are excluded from the definition of service provider.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in Hoboken.
rules.quoted_span: they can no longer use software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.

rules.title: Tenant request for legal rent calculation
rules.requirement: A tenant may request a legal rent calculation when the tenant believes the rent exceeds the legal rent.
rules.key_value: Right to request a legal rent calculation
rules.quoted_span:
A tenant may request a legal rent calculation where the
tenant's rent is believed to be in excess of the legal rent as established
pursuant to the ordinance.

rules.title: Original-tenant designation and vacancy decontrol
rules.requirement: A landlord renting an apartment to multiple tenants may designate all members of the original tenant group as original tenants; vacancy is deemed to occur when the last original tenant leaves, allowing the landlord to seek available vacancy-decontrol relief.
rules.key_value: Vacancy is deemed to occur when the last original tenant vacates
rules.citation: Hoboken Rent Control Regulations, Regulation #3: Vacancy Decontrol as to Multiple Tenants
rules.quoted_span:
a landlord who rents a residential apartment unit to
multiple tenants may designate an original tenant category which shall consist of all the members
of the original group of tenants to which the unit is rented.

rules.title: Timely vacancy-decontrol certificate
rules.requirement: A landlord may file a decontrol certificate for a year it legally owned the dwelling, no later than one year after the later of the vacancy or first rental to a replacement tenant; the dwelling must be registered, and filing must precede a legal-rent-calculation request for the certificate to be used in a legal rent determination.
rules.key_value: No later than one year after the later of vacancy or first rental to a replacement tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: The dwelling must be registered when the certificate is filed; certificate use in a legal rent determination also requires filing before a request for a legal rent calculation.
rules.quoted_span:
A Landlord of any dwelling subject to the provisions of this chapter may file a Certificate
pursuant to Section 155-33 for any year where the landlord legally owned the dwelling, provided
the Certificate is filed no later than the latter of either one (1) year from when the vacancy
occurred or one (1) year from when the apartment was first rented to a replacement Tenant after
a vacancy

rules.title: Mandatory disclosure for rent increases
rules.requirement: With any lease or written notice of rent increase for a residential dwelling unit, the landlord must provide a sworn disclosure statement, executed under penalty of perjury and substantially in the prescribed form. The form certifies that no entity exchanged anything of value for a Service Provider’s services in connection with the proposed rent, that the rent-increase methodology did not use shared non-public competitor data, and includes the stated acknowledgment concerning illegal deception, fraud, misrepresentation, or knowing failure or refusal to provide important information.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to a lease or written notice of rent increase for a residential dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span:
Any landlord must include, with any lease or written notice of rent increase for a residential dwelling unit, a sworn
disclosure statement, executed under penalty of perjury, in substantially the following form:
